data.title: Authority Impersonation and Payment Fraud Susceptibility
data.summary: Requests appearing to originate from senior staff produced action without out-of-band verification, including changes to payment details and the release of sensitive data. Pressure, urgency and seniority were sufficient to bypass the documented process.
data.description:
Business email compromise is the highest-value social engineering attack precisely because it targets process rather than technology. There is no payload to detect: a plausible message, from a plausible sender, asking for something the recipient has done before.

Its effectiveness rests on psychological levers that are difficult to resist at an individual level — authority, urgency, confidentiality ("do not discuss this, it is not announced yet"), and the scarcity of time. Staff who recognise the pattern in training still comply in the moment, because refusing means challenging a senior person on the basis of a suspicion.

Reconnaissance makes it credible: public announcements, travel visible on social media, organisational charts and supplier relationships supply the details that make the request fit. Supplier impersonation — a bank detail change on an invoice from a real supplier — is the variant that most often succeeds, because the relationship is genuine.
data.recommendation:
* Require out-of-band verification, through a known number never taken from the request, for any payment, bank detail change or bulk data release — regardless of who appears to be asking.
* Make the verification step mandatory and non-waivable, so no one may authorise skipping it; this removes the individual's burden of refusal.
* Separate duties so that no single person can both change payment details and release payment.
* Flag external mail, and monitor for look-alike domains of your own and your suppliers'.
* Rehearse the scenario with finance and executive assistants specifically, including the pressure, so the first encounter is not the real one.
data.short_recommendation: Require out-of-band verification for payment and data changes.
